construction_notes: Descriptor repair only, in the write-only phase. The previous build ran to completion, wrote public/train.csv, public/eval.csv and private/holdout.csv, and the worker failed afterwards at the qualification gate with a single failed check, timing.prediction_time_declared, whose detail was that quality.json carried no task.prediction_time. Root cause: the saved quality object had no task block at all, so the gate could not read prediction_time even though the same wording existed in the research plan. Correction: quality now carries a complete task descriptor - question, decision_user, population, prediction_time, target, the eleven concrete feature descriptions, usefulness, simple_references, split_policy and outcome_horizon - with prediction_time stated as the series begin date, the same decision instant already used by split assignment and by the shipped begin carry column. The description of population, split_policy and target restates the rules the build already enforces (agency USGS, parameter 00060, statistic 00003, daily values, primary series, begin 2001-01-01 to 2019-12-31, non-null end, state codes outside 81-86 and 90-98, earliest series per location, 365 day continuation exclusion, 60 day embargo gaps). No build code changes: URLs, download parsing, population, label rule, feature construction and split boundaries are untouched, and no check was removed or relaxed to force success. Missing metadata still stays missing rather than becoming zero, null-end series are dropped rather than imputed, and the regional termination rate uses only series that begin before 2013-01-01 and whose fifth anniversary and recorded end both precede the scored row, so matured eval and holdout labels never enter a training or scored rate. references is unchanged: no per-entity persistence column applies because each location contributes exactly one row and no shipped column records that location own earlier outcome, so persistence_column stays null and entity_columns name the state, district and hydrologic region identity columns for a train-only reference. Unverified points stand and are stated as assumptions: current-vintage site attributes are assumed to describe the site near establishment, the 365 day exclusion cannot see sibling series that began before 2001, instantaneous-series query completeness is assumed, and training label timing is unverified because no full-row availability ledger exists, so the task remains retrospective_research rather than a forecasting claim. Two wording fixes avoid prose that pairs a field name with an equals sign: the source limitation now says USGS agency filter and the reason text says restricting to USGS agency records, keeping the same field references and the same filtering rule. No source snapshot was re-read in this phase; all statements about the publisher reuse the evidence entries already recorded.

cross_row_audit.auxiliary_files_review: Only train.csv, eval.csv and holdout.csv are written under the output directory; no fixture labels, answer scaffolds or auxiliary evaluation files.
cross_row_audit.rationale: Rows are distinct monitoring locations, so a location never appears in two splits and no row outcome window is another row input. The regional rate is deliberately restricted to series beginning before the training boundary so matured eval and holdout labels cannot leak into a scored row.

altitude.availability: site attribute that is null for some sites; assumed stable since establishment, current-vintage value

begin.availability: period-of-record start carried on the time-series metadata record and equal to the decision instant

begin_month.availability: derived from the begin date itself, so available exactly at the decision instant

contributing_drainage_area.availability: site attribute that is frequently null; assumed present at establishment where the publisher reports it, never filled with zero

district_code.availability: USGS Water Science Center district code recorded with the site; assumed to reflect the operating office at establishment, though offices are reorganised over time

drainage_area.availability: site attribute carried on the current record; assumed to describe the site at establishment, but the value may have been entered or revised after the record opened, and nulls stay missing

end.availability: period-of-record end used only to build the label and to test whether a neighbour series was active at the decision instant

has_instantaneous_discharge_series.availability: constructed from a second metadata query, counting only instantaneous series whose begin is on or before the daily-mean begin date, so it is observable at the decision instant

huc2_prior_termination_rate.availability: constructed only from series that begin before 2013-01-01 and whose fifth anniversary preceded the decision date, with an end already recorded before it; scored eval and holdout labels never enter the rate

huc2_region.availability: first two digits of the hydrologic unit code recorded with the site; assumed fixed at establishment

monitoring_location_id.availability: stable site identifier assigned at establishment and returned on every metadata record

nearby_active_gage_count_50km.availability: constructed from point geometry and per-series begin and end, counting only series with begin at or before the decision date and end at or after it; restricted to series present in this extract, so pre-2001 neighbours are invisible

site_type_code.availability: hydrologic setting code recorded with the site; assumed fixed at establishment

state_code.availability: administrative state code recorded with the site; assumed fixed at establishment

limitations: Current-vintage retrospective design: drainage area, contributing area, altitude, site type, state, district and the primary flag are read from the current record, not an archived 2001-2019 snapshot, so their operational availability at establishment is unverified.
The label is record continuation, not physical gage survival: a series can end because publication changed, the site converted to stage-only, or the record moved to another agency.

The 365 day continuation exclusion can only see sibling series that begin inside the 2001-2019 download window, so a location whose earlier series began before 2001 and overlapped the new begin date cannot be detected from this extract.
The nearby gage count and the regional termination rate are computed from series present in this single download, which excludes cooperating-agency records and series beginning outside the window.
No full-row availability ledger exists, so training label timing is unverified and the task is not a forecasting claim.
Missing site metadata such as drainage area, contributing area and altitude stay missing rather than being imputed as zero.

selection.evidence: Eligibility is decided only from record facts readable on the begin date: agency, parameter, statistic, data type, begin, state code and the presence of an end value. Features use site metadata plus two network reconstructions that read only series active or already ended at or before the begin date. No outcome value selects rows. The shipped begin column is the decision instant itself, known when the record opens; only the recorded end enters the label as a post-outcome observation compared with the fifth anniversary of begin.
selection.outcome_conditioning: Rows with a null end timestamp are excluded because the label cannot be computed; that is conditioning on label availability, not on the label value.

vintage.evidence: The combined-metadata collection returns the current record for each site; no archived 2001-2019 snapshot of site attributes or series metadata is published.

external_threshold.source: Five-year continuation horizon fixed by the frozen task as the calendar fifth anniversary of the series begin date, before any scoring

measurements.frame: USGS site attribute, area upstream of the gage
USGS site attribute, contributing area when it differs from the total
USGS site attribute, gage or land surface altitude on the recorded vertical datum
count of distinct other USGS locations with a daily-mean discharge series active on the decision date within 50 km by haversine
share of training-window daily-mean series in the same hydrologic region whose fifth anniversary preceded the decision date and whose record had already ended
calendar month of the series begin date

construction.access_recipe: 1) GET the combined-metadata URL with parameter_code 00060, data_type Daily values, agency_code USGS and begin 2001-01-01/2019-12-31, following links with rel next until no next link remains and caching each page. 2) Flatten each feature: keep site properties and expand only the nested time-series list whose items carry begin, end, parameter_code, statistic_id or data_type; ignore unrelated nested lists. Use GeoJSON geometry coordinates when present and longitude and latitude properties otherwise. 3) Keep USGS rows with parameter 00060, statistic 00003, a daily data type, a primary series, a begin inside 2001-01-01 to 2019-12-31, a non-null end, and a state code outside 81-86 and 90-98. 4) Deduplicate to the earliest qualifying series per location and drop a location when another daily series was active in the prior 365 days. 5) Build the label from begin and end date arithmetic only. 6) Query the combined-metadata collection for parameter 00060 instantaneous series, first with statistic_id 00011 and, if that returns no features, with data_type Instantaneous values; build the flag only from series whose begin is on or before the daily begin date. 7) Count distinct other locations with a daily series active at the decision date within 50 km by haversine, excluding the row own location by identifier. 8) Build the regional termination rate only from series that begin before 2013-01-01, whose fifth anniversary is on or before the decision date, and whose end is before the decision date; scored eval and holdout labels never enter the rate. 9) Assign half-open splits by begin date with 60 day embargo gaps and write train, eval and holdout.
construction.expected_size: Explicitly estimated, not measured: the service does not return numberMatched for this collection. Nationwide there are on the order of 25,000-30,000 parameter-00060 time series (all statistics, all agencies); the 2001-2019 daily-mean begin window is estimated at roughly 8,000-12,000 USGS locations after deduplication. Raw JSON pages on the order of 30-80 MB; final modeling table roughly 8k-12k rows by about 15 columns. Sample cohorts observed on 2026-11-15 showed a five-year continuation rate near 40-60%, so no severe class imbalance.
construction.format: OGC API features (GeoJSON pages) from api.waterdata.usgs.gov, parsed to a flat CSV for the benchmark; CSV output is also advertised by the service as an alternate link, but JSON paging is the verified path.
construction.source_examples: Observed on 2026-11-15 via the filtered endpoint: USGS-08025500 'Bayou Toro near Toro, LA' has begin 1955-10-01, end 2026-11-13, statistic_id 00003, data_type 'Daily values', unit ft^3/s, drainage_area 148.0, state Louisiana. USGS-05579725 'LITTLE KICKAPOO CREEK NEAR HEYWORTH, IL' has begin 2005-05-26, end 2026-11-13, drainage_area 24.9. USGS-03236800 'Salt Creek at Richmond Dale OH' has begin 2005-07-01, end 2007-08-31, drainage_area 552.0 - an example of a record that fails the five-year test. USGS-02264141 shows a null altitude and null drainage area, confirming that missing metadata must be handled rather than assumed present.

limitations: Current-vintage retrospective design: drainage area, altitude, site type and the primary approval flag are read from today's record, not from an archived 2001-2019 snapshot. They are plausible establishment-time attributes but this does not prove historical operational availability.

A daily mean discharge series can end because publication changed (gage continues with stage only, converts to instantaneous-only, or is transferred to another agency), not only because the physical gage closed. The label is record continuation, not infrastructure survival.

Series with internal gaps count as continued if the last observation passes the fifth anniversary; no data-completeness threshold is applied, which the next task may add as a documented secondary variant.
USGS `begin` dates for older or migrated sites can reflect data-system history rather than the first day of physical operation; restricting to 2001-2019 reduces but does not eliminate this.
Cooperating-agency and non-USGS records are excluded by the USGS agency filter, so the population is USGS-operated records only; this also keeps the statutory public-domain basis clean.
17 U.S.C. 105 is a U.S.-law exclusion and the legislative history states it has no effect on protection abroad; we claim U.S. public-domain status only and assert no worldwide dedication.
Unauthenticated API rate limits apply; an api_key may be needed for bulk paging, and the service's page size and cursor behaviour should be handled defensively rather than assumed.

Labels freeze at the 2026-11-15 snapshot; all outcome windows close by 2024-12-31, so late data revisions should not change this cohort's labels, but a later rebuild will produce a slightly different population.

State and district features partly encode funding and program shocks, so the task measures administrative persistence as well as hydrologic or infrastructure factors; no causal interpretation is warranted.
source.reason: The USGS Water Data OGC API exposes a single machine-readable collection (combined-metadata) that carries, per monitoring location, both site attributes (drainage area, altitude, HUC, state, site type, agency) and the exact period of record (begin/end) of each daily mean discharge time series. That supports a one-row-per-location forward task whose label is a later observation date rather than a copied field, with no accounts, no joins across agencies, and no personal data. Reuse rests on a verified statutory basis (17 U.S.C. 105(a)) plus the publisher's own statement that USGS-produced data are in the U.S. public domain; restricting to USGS agency records keeps third-party cooperating-agency records out of scope.

task.outcome_horizon: Five years from the first day of record (calendar fifth anniversary; about 1,826 days).
task.population: USGS monitoring locations (agency code USGS) in the 50 states, DC and territories, excluding ANSI state codes 81 to 86 and 90 to 98 used for Mexican and Canadian subdivisions, that carry a primary daily mean discharge series (parameter 00060, statistic 00003, data type daily values) whose begin falls between 2001-01-01 and 2019-12-31. One row per location, taking the earliest such series. A location is excluded when another 00060 daily mean series at the same location was active at any time in the 365 days before that begin. Series with a null end are dropped.
task.prediction_time: The series begin date (first day of the daily mean discharge record), using only site metadata and facts about the record and the surrounding network at the moment it opens; no later observation of that same series is used as an input.
task.question: When a new USGS daily mean streamflow record opens at a monitoring location, will that record still be active five years later?
task.simple_references: Majority class; begin-year cohort base rate; state and district identity rate learned from training rows only; and a two-rule heuristic combining drainage area above the training median with the instantaneous series flag. Persistence of the entity's own prior outcome does not apply because each location contributes one row.
task.split_policy: Chronological by `begin` date: train 2001-01-01 to 2012-12-31; eval 2013-01-01 to 2015-12-31; holdout 2016-01-01 to 2019-12-31. A 60-day embargo gap is dropped immediately after each boundary (2013-01-01 to 2013-03-01 and 2016-01-01 to 2016-03-01) so multi-site installation projects do not straddle splits. Rows are distinct locations, so no location appears in more than one split and no row's outcome window is another row's input.
task.target: The label continued_5y is 1 when the time series end timestamp (most recent observation in that series) is on or after the fifth anniversary of begin, and 0 otherwise. Series with no end value are dropped, never imputed.
task.usefulness: The label is a future state of the record rather than a field copied from the row; it separates gages that become multi-decade series from short-lived project or miscellaneous records, which matters for weighting records in trend and load models and for setting cooperator expectations at installation. Inputs mix basin size, program identity and network context, leaving honest baselines real headroom.

prediction_instant.citation: The decision instant is the record begin date read from the same metadata feature; the publisher documents no reporting period or publication lag for it, so no lag value is asserted.

row_selection.rule: Eligible when agency is USGS, parameter is 00060, statistic is 00003, data type is daily values, begin falls inside 2001-01-01 to 2019-12-31, end is present, and the state code is outside 81-86 and 90-98. Series with a null end are dropped because the label cannot be formed; that conditions on label availability, not on label value.
